title: RabakBench: Scaling Human Annotations to Construct Localized Multilingual Safety Benchmarks for Low-Resource Languages

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating 11 open-source and closed-source safety guardrail classifiers on a newly constructed multilingual dataset containing 5,364 examples across four low-resource languages/creoles (Singlish, Chinese, Malay, and Tamil) to measure performance degradation and inconsistencies compared to standard high-resource languages.

Using LLM-driven adversarial red-teaming and real-world local web content to generate test cases featuring culturally specific phenomena such as code-mixing, localized euphemistic slang, and regional references (specifically localized to Singapore) to evaluate whether models miss culturally-specific harms or falsely flag benign cultural phrases.

Evaluating safety classifiers against a fine-grained harm taxonomy that includes a 'Hate' category, testing the models' ability to accurately detect discriminatory statements and explicit hate speech targeting protected demographic groups (e.g., race, religion, descent) within the localized Singaporean context.
